title: The M4+ share stayed near 1 percent in a north Oklahoma–south Kansas box, but the 2020–2025 sample was small
abstract: We test a size signature of density-driven pressure after disposal cuts in the published north Oklahoma–south Kansas box. USGS ComCat has 2,996 M2.5+ events in 2013–2018 and 103 in 2020–2025, with 28 and one M4+ events. The M4+ share ratio is 1.039. The exact independent-event odds-ratio interval is 0.025–6.416. The data do not resolve enrichment and cannot exclude a large increase. The M3.5+ share ratio is 1.385, with results that depend on the reference test and base threshold. Median preferred depth rises from 5.63 to 7.00 km, while median reported depth error falls from 5.9 to 0.4 km and the preferred network changes. This prevents a simple depth comparison from isolating migration. The result does not identify the residual driver or test the ETAS taper. It supplies a fixed-box later-period audit, aggregate evidence, source hashes and reproducible code. Source earthquake records remain outside the baseline package.

display.caption: Annual counts, high-magnitude shares and preferred-depth quality in the published box. Zero counts are retained. Error values are catalog reports, not a calibration of actual location error.

citations.reason: Published study box and later size-signature test; no flow model was fitted.
